scope.flow: ProgressiveCurve.previewWithdraw (and OffsetProgressiveCurve.previewWithdraw) full-withdrawal preview via BondingCurveRegistry.previewWithdraw
scope.environment: Solidity protocol curves (ProgressiveCurve.sol, OffsetProgressiveCurve.sol) using PCMath fixed-point math

entities.name: External integration / UI / on-chain contract caller

statements.text: The previewWithdraw call is a full withdrawal where assets == totalAssets.
The supplied inputs are valid, i.e. assets <= totalAssets.
The curve state satisfies totalAssets ≈ HALF_SLOPE * totalShares².
A caller invokes BondingCurveRegistry.previewWithdraw, which delegates to ProgressiveCurve.previewWithdraw (or OffsetProgressiveCurve.previewWithdraw).

previewWithdraw computes deduct with ceiling division (PCMath.divUp) while PCMath.square(s) uses floor rounding (mul(x,x)), so deduct = ceil(totalAssets / HALF_SLOPE) can exceed floor(totalShares²) by 1 ULP and the sub() underflows.
For a full withdrawal, previewWithdraw(totalAssets, totalAssets, totalShares) should return totalShares.
previewWithdraw should never revert for valid inputs where assets <= totalAssets.
The rounding used in previewWithdraw should be consistent (floor) so that the ceiling-divided deduct does not exceed the floor-rounded square term.

ambiguities: Report does not state who may call previewWithdraw or any authorization requirement; caller is a generic external integration/UI/contract.
The exact numeric values of totalAssets, totalShares and HALF_SLOPE are not given; only the approximate relationship and 1 ULP excess are stated.
Whether the revert occurs for the specific full-withdrawal case is stated as 'can exceed ... causing revert', a conditional/potential outcome.
